episodes.194051: Scattered thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee on September 1, 2024. Lightning with one of these thunderstorms reportedly struck a man near Antioch.
episodes.194304: A slowly-passing cold front combined with adequate instability to produce several strong afternoon thunderstorms across far southeastern central Indiana.  One cell towered high enough to trigger a brief microburst over west-central Jennings County.
episodes.194357: Modest height falls as a slow moving shortwave trough crossed the region resulted in a few strong to severe storms ahead of a surface cold front. Strongest shear (25-30kts) was observed largely south of Pittsburgh allowing for more organized convection and a heightened severe threat.
episodes.195228: Thunderstorm activity developed across the higher terrain and foothills north and east of the Phoenix metro area during the afternoon hours of the 1st and moved southwestward towards the Phoenix East Valley before weakening. The thunderstorms were instigated by large scale forcing for ascent from an upper-level low moving over southern AZ as well as MLCAPE values of 500 J/KG. DCAPE values were in excess of 1500 J/KG and thus conditions were ideal for these thunderstorms to produce strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.195397: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced very localized wind damage in Orange County, Virginia.
episodes.195699: Ahead of a cold front advancing southward from the Ohio Valley, storms developed along a surface trough and progressed east and southeast. Isolated storms formed in the late afternoon over the eastern Piedmont and Triangle to central Coastal Plain. A second batch of storms developed over the western part of the state and tracked into the Piedmont in the evening hours. Several storms produced severe gusts and isolated flash flooding.
episodes.195722: A complex frontal system stalled over the Central Southern Tier of New York during the late afternoon and evening. This system triggered slow moving, heavy rain producing thunderstorms in the Elmira-Horseheads area which caused areas of flash flooding on area roads and small streams.
episodes.195829: A cluster of storms moving onshore produced a strong wind gust in Martin County.
episodes.195830: Storms produced heavy rainfall and flooded homes and businesses in Orlando.
episodes.195994: Showers and thunderstorms developed over the region within a warm and moist airmass on the east side of a cold front. A few of these thunderstorms increased to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts with trees being blown down.  One line of storms developed across the northern half of Tazewell County, producing downpours at rates of three to locally five inches per hour. Crest Unit Streamflow north of the Town of Tazewell was indicating returns of between 600 and 750 cfs per mi^2, with three-hour average recurrence intervals of between 75 an 130 years.
episodes.195997: Showers and thunderstorms developed out ahead of an incoming surface trough across the Coastal Plain late in the morning across the Coastal Plain. This shower and thunderstorm activity then pushed east and strengthened with a few of these storms becoming strong to severe in nature bringing a damaging wind threat to the Albemarle Sound and our northern waters during the afternoon on September first.
episodes.196222: A cold front moving through a warm and unstable air mass produced strong to severe thunderstorms over portions of Lake Superior on the 31st.
episodes.196228: A cold front moving through a warm and unstable air mass produced a strong thunderstorm at Minneapolis Shoal Light in the Bay of Green Bay on the 31st.
episodes.196573: A significant heavy rainfall event occurred early in the month across mainly the Concho Valley, northern Heartland and southern Big Country due to a slow moving upper level storm system and a very moist tropical airmass, which was near record levels for early September. Numerous showers and a few thunderstorms produced localized heavy rainfall amounts greater than 10 inches across portions of northeast Tom Green, southwest Runnels and northern Concho counties which resulted in significant areal and flash flooding.
episodes.196584: A complex of thunderstorms dropped southeast into north Alabama from middle and western Tennessee during the midday hours. A well defined gust front pushed south from these thunderstorms producing strong and gusty winds. A couple of trees were knocked down as a result in Colbert County.
episodes.196689: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across northeast Georgia throughout the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Habersham County.
episodes.196690: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina throughout the afternoon into the evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in the Charlotte area.
episodes.196946: A marginal risk for severe weather was posted across the SE CONUS ahead of a weak frontal boundary. Damaging winds were the main thunderstorm threat.
episodes.196947: Strong to severe thunderstorms formed ahead of a weak frontal boundary with gusty winds over marine areas.

On September 1st, people on Jaluit Atoll, within the Marshall islands, reported damage due to a brief period of strong winds. Satellite imagery around the estimated time of damage, which was between 1200LST (1000ChST) and 1300LST (1100ChST), showed building cumulus and cumulonimbus near the atoll, suggesting the potential of a gust front or outflow boundary causing the damage. A Marshallese governmental PMU unit did an assessment and found 8 homes and 3 churches were damaged and initial reports suggest 43.3 Thousand $USD will be allocated to support the affected community. Photos taken of the damage showed tin roofs that were nailed to simple structures were either stripped off the roof or one side of the tin roof remained attached and the rest was rolled up by the wind. A few broadleaf (palm) trees were also shown to be blown down by the winds. Initial reports from Jaluit speculated that the damage was done by a tornado or waterspout. However, statements from the atoll do not mention a funnel or waterspout being reported, and some reports conflicting information. Some reported blues and then it suddenly became windy, while others said it was cloudy and raining when the strong winds occurred.  Since there are no firm statements of anyone claiming to have seen a funnel or waterspout, and damage reports cannot conclusively support a tornado or waterspout, this event is currently contributed to thunderstorms winds (outflow) though a tornado/waterspout cannot be ruled out completely.
